translation_notes: The original builds its query text by splicing already-bracketed IRI syntax (EX_A = "<http://example/a>") straight into an f-string, not by interpolating a data value in term position. s{ }'s {expr} holes are never textual substitution: interpolating {EX_A} would coerce the Python string "<http://example/a>" into a Literal via initBindings, not the URIRef the bracket syntax denotes -- silently wrong for a query built to test ground-pattern matching. Since the three IRIs are compile-time constants here, not data, the faithful translation writes them directly as terms in the island, losing the EX_A/EX_B/EX_NOPE indirection the original used purely to avoid retyping the fragment across five sibling tests in the same file. What is missing: a way to splice already-formed island syntax (an IRI, a whole triple pattern) from a Python-level constant into s{ }, short of writing it out again at each use site.
